- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.23) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.11) and prices are trending up, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid premature bearish bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overestimates continuation — reduce forecast slope or add a ceiling to prevent overshoot.  
- Model consistently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — if recent 18-day average is > 65, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% to reflect momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model tends to lag in recognizing reversal — add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast to capture sentiment-driven rebound.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period volatility — increase final 5–7 days’ forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for sentiment-driven volatility clustering.
